table.name: conductor
table.purpose: A directory of orchestra conductors: each row is one conductor with their age, nationality, and years of work (tenure/experience). Referenced by the orchestra table, which assigns a conductor to each orchestra.

Age.name: Age
Age.description: Age of the conductor in years (range 40-63).

Conductor_ID.name: Conductor_ID
Conductor_ID.description: Primary key identifying each conductor; referenced one-to-one by orchestra.Conductor_ID.

Name.name: Name
Name.description: Full name of the conductor (e.g. 'Pierre Boulez', 'Colin Davis').

Nationality.name: Nationality
Nationality.description: Country of nationality of the conductor, as a short code/name (USA, UK, France).

Year_of_Work.name: Year_of_Work
Year_of_Work.description: Number of years the conductor has worked (tenure/experience), range 6-21. The column name suggests a calendar year, but the values (6-21) clearly indicate a count of years rather than a year; the table's purpose confirms it records years of work.

table.name: orchestra
table.purpose: Catalog of orchestras, each with its principal conductor, record company, main recording format, and founding year of the ensemble (or of its recording relationship). One row per orchestra.

Conductor_ID.name: Conductor ID
Conductor_ID.description: Reference to conductor.Conductor_ID, identifying the conductor associated with this orchestra (one-to-one).

Major_Record_Format.name: Major record format
Major_Record_Format.description: Physical format(s) in which the orchestra's recordings were primarily issued: CD, LP (vinyl), or DVD.

Orchestra.name: Orchestra name
Orchestra.description: Full name of the orchestra (e.g., Chicago Symphony Orchestra, London Symphony Orchestra).

Orchestra_ID.name: Orchestra ID
Orchestra_ID.description: Primary key of the orchestra table; referenced by performance.Orchestra_ID.

Record_Company.name: Record company
Record_Company.description: Record label(s) the orchestra recorded with (e.g., Decca Records, Deutsche Grammophon); occasionally two labels combined.

Year_of_Founded.name: Year of founded
Year_of_Founded.description: Year the orchestra was founded, stored as a number. Note: values (2002-2009) are implausibly recent for these historic orchestras, so it may instead record the year of a particular recording or of the row's data entry; the exact meaning is uncertain.

table.name: performance
table.purpose: TV broadcast performance records: one row per episode/broadcast of a talent-show-style series (auditions, semi-finals, final), with UK-style official viewing figures (ratings in millions, audience share, weekly rank) and an associated orchestra. Referenced by show and linked to orchestra.

Date.name: Broadcast date
Date.description: Day and month of the broadcast (year omitted). Values like '10 June', '16 June'; one date ('17 June') appears twice, likely two broadcasts that day (e.g. final and results show).

Official_ratings_(millions).name: Official ratings (millions of viewers)
Official_ratings_(millions).description: Official audience measurement for the broadcast, in millions of viewers (5.2 to 11.58, mean ~8.4).

Orchestra_ID.name: Orchestra ID
Orchestra_ID.description: Foreign key to orchestra.Orchestra_ID, identifying the orchestra associated with this performance/episode.

Performance_ID.name: Performance ID
Performance_ID.description: Primary key of the table; identifier of the performance/episode, referenced by show.Performance_ID.

Share.name: Audience share
Share.description: Percentage of total TV audience watching this broadcast (stored as text with '%' sign), 22.7% to 43.7%.

Type.name: Episode type
Type.description: Stage of the competition the broadcast covers: 'Auditions 1'–'5', 'Semi-final 3', 'Live final results', 'Series average'.

Weekly_rank.name: Weekly rank
Weekly_rank.description: The broadcast's ranking among all TV programmes that week (stored as text; includes 'TBC' = to be confirmed).

table.name: show
table.purpose: Despite the name 'show', the values (Scottish football grounds like Hampden Park, Fir Park, St. Mirren Park, plus attendance figures and T/F results) indicate this table records football matches: one row per match, with the venue, attendance, result (win/loss flag), and a link to a performance (match date). The naming appears to be a disguised/renamed sports dataset rather than concert shows. Only 5 rows are visible, so the broader scope is tentative. The 'If_first_show' column holding venue names suggests the table may specifically track whether a match was the first show/fixture at a given ground, but the evidence is thin.

Attendance.name: Attendance
Attendance.description: Match attendance (number of spectators), ranging 555–2431 in the sample. Declared DOUBLE but integer-valued.

If_first_show.name: Venue
If_first_show.description: Name of the stadium/venue where the event took place (Glebe Park, Fir Park, St. Mirren Park, Hampden Park — all Scottish football grounds). The joined performance table records TV broadcast episodes, which does not clarify the venue semantics; the column name suggests it may flag the venue of a first show, but the values are simply venue names, so the exact intent remains tentative.

Performance_ID.name: Performance_ID
Performance_ID.description: Foreign key to performance.Performance_ID, identifying the date/performance this match belongs to (one-to-one).

Result.name: Result
Result.description: Boolean flag (T/F), most plausibly whether the match result was a win (T) or not (F). Could alternatively mean e.g. home win vs. loss; the joined performance table (TV broadcast records) provides no additional evidence to disambiguate the semantics.

Show_ID.name: Show_ID
Show_ID.description: Primary key of the table; unique identifier for each match/show record.
